title: Protegga il giusto cielo
subtitle: Donna Anna, Donna Elvira and Don Ottavio: the trio of the masks in the finale from Don Giovanni, Act 1 (No. 13)

licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score, with its repeats (Don Ottavio's il zelo, il zelo del mio cor; Donna Elvira's tradito, tradito, il mio, il mio and vendichi, vendichi). The first bar carries Leporello's -mor!, the end of d'amor from the piece before; it is played but is not part of this piece's words.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 124–126, the Adagio of No. 13 (from page 124, system 3, bar 2, to the last bar of page 126), 22 bars
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by a fresh checker. The first bar is shared with the piece before (Presto, presto, pria ch'ei venga): it holds Leporello's last syllable, -mor!, and the three masked guests begin in bar 2. Don Ottavio's part, printed in the treble clef, is written at sounding pitch. Donna Anna's small-print turns in bars 11 and 15 and Donna Elvira's small notes in bars 7 and 10 are grace notes, as printed. Bars 21–22 are for the piano alone. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Adagio, cut time (2/2), B-flat major throughout. Playback tempo ♩ = 38 (a half note ≈ 19), from the median track time, 2:20, of five complete recordings that give the trio its own track (Giulini 1959 2:19, Klemperer 1966 2:20, Barenboim 1975 2:29, Haitink 1984 2:32, I. Fischer 2026 2:08); Mozart gives the word Adagio only.
